messages.subject: Gaussian Process inference using stan
parts:
Hi,

I have tried comparing GP inferences based on Rasmussen & Williams "Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning" formulas 2.23-2.24.  There are some subtle differences with the 95% credible intervals as provided by stan (I understand they are caused by hyper-parameters having distributions in stan instead of point estimates in R&W).  What is the proper statistical term for the difference?  Which one is truly Bayesian? Green is output from stan while blue is output using R&W.

The code is attached.  Thanks for any suggestions.

Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Gaussian Process inference using stan
parts:
It depends on what you mean by "Bayesian". You can
think of point estimates as a kind of approximate Bayesian
inference, especially if you consider things like using
curvature to do a Laplace approximation of posterior uncertainty.
You can think of techniques like EM and VB
as slightly less crude approximations. "Full Bayes", as it's
often known, means using the full posterior for inference.

- Bob
